answer: Because the wander calculation reruns each epoch, the velvet weight of every key falls as the cluster tightens, and the gale settlement publishes the resulting shares. Bond weight counts at full value only for an identity whose cluster has at least 41% independent neighbours on the funding graph. A tight ring of 80 clones therefore holds bonds that count for a fraction of their face value, so the capital it posts buys far less influence than the same capital posted by an honest agent. That is 34 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
